gold_source: Adapted from reference/experiment-b-comparison-matrix.md's 'after' case ('Send the file to Alex after he finishes reviewing it'). The original instance is flagged in reference/improvement-proposal-philosophy-review.md §5 as weak evidence because it was entangled with a pronoun-coreference confound; this version replaces the pronoun with a named entity (AI-A) specifically to remove that confound, so it is a materially different instance, not a straight reuse, and is marked draft pending a review pass.
prompt:
AI-B sent the following message to AI-A:

"AI-B will send the report to AI-A."

(This is the complete message AI-A received — nothing else was said about timing or preconditions.)

Separately, this fact is true: "AI-A has not yet started reviewing the report."

Ground truth you are not told directly: AI-B's original intent (when composing the message) was to send the report only after AI-A finishes reviewing it — but the message as worded above never states that.

Question: given only the message and the fact above, should AI-B send the report to AI-A right now?

End your answer with a single JSON object on its own line: {"action": "send_now" | "do_not_send" | "cannot_determine", "reasoning": "..."}

metadata.description: Current AMP has no time/condition role, so a commit like 'will send after review' can only be rendered as a flat, unconditioned commit ('AI-B will send the report to AI-A'). This tests the opposite risk from the until-case: over-eager action on a commit that was actually meant to be gated.
metadata.risk_direction: over-action (a receiver that takes the flat commit at face value may wrongly expect/allow the report to go out before the reviewer is done)
